}}'''Lucia Francisca''' "'''Susi'''" '''Susanti Haditono''' ({{lang-zh|s=王蓮香|p=Wáng Liánxiāng|poj=Ông Liân-hiang}}; born 11 February 1971) is an Indonesian retired [[badminton]] player.<ref>[http://www.olympic.org/susi-susanti olympic.org]</ref> Relatively small of stature, she combined quick and graceful movement with elegant shotmaking technique, and is regarded by many as one of the greatest women's singles players of all time.<ref>{{cite web|last=Leigh|first=James|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/badminton-shock-defeat-for-susanti-1620396.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220525/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/badminton-shock-defeat-for-susanti-1620396.html |archive-date=25 May 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live|title=Badminton: Shock defeat for Susanti|website=[[The Independent]]|date=21 May 1995|access-date=22 October 2018}}</ref> She was the inaugural [[Badminton at the Summer Olympics|Olympic]] women's badminton champion and the first Indonesian Olympic gold medalist.

== Career ==
Susanti won the women's singles gold medal at the [[Badminton at the 1992 Summer Olympics|1992 Olympic Games]] in Barcelona, Spain and the bronze medal at the [[Badminton at the 1996 Summer Olympics|1996 Olympic Games]] in Atlanta, United States. She retired from the world badminton circuit not long after her marriage, in February 1997, to [[Alan Budikusuma]], who had also won a badminton singles gold medal at the 1992 Summer Olympics. Susanti was the most dominant women's singles player in the first half of the 1990s, winning the [[All England Open Badminton Championships|All England Open]] in 1990, 1991, 1993 and 1994, the [[World Badminton Grand Prix Finals]] five consecutive times from 1990 to 1994 as well as in 1996, and the [[BWF World Championships|IBF World Championships]] in 1993. She is the only female player to hold the Olympic, World Championship, and All-England singles titles simultaneously. She won the [[Japan Open (badminton)|Japan Open]] three times and the [[Indonesia Open (badminton)|Indonesian Open]] six times. She also won numerous Badminton Grand Prix series events and five [[Badminton World Cup]]s. She led the Indonesian team to victory over perennial champion [[China national badminton team|China]] in the [[1994 Uber Cup|1994]] and [[1996 Uber Cup]] (women's world team) competitions. All of this came during a relatively strong period in women's international badminton. Her chief competitors early in her prime years were the Chinese players [[Tang Jiuhong]] and [[Huang Hua (badminton)|Huang Hua]], and, later, China's [[Ye Zhaoying]] and the Korean [[Bang Soo-hyun]].

Susanti was inducted into the [[International Badminton Federation]] (IBF, currently [[Badminton World Federation|BWF]]) [[World Badminton Hall of Fame|Hall of Fame]] in May 2004, and received the [[Herbert Scheele Trophy]] in 2002. She lit the flame at the [[2018 Asian Games]] opening ceremony.

== Playing style ==
Susanti was an extremely durable defensive player who liked to instigate long rallies to wear down her opponent's stamina and invite errors. That style was in contrast to most of the top female players of her time such as [[Bang Soo-hyun]], [[Tang Jiuhong]], [[Huang Hua (badminton)|Huang Hua]], and [[Ye Zhaoying]], who employed a more aggressive style.

Susanti's matches against top-tier opponents were characteristically slow-paced and long, especially in the era of 15 points system when a player could only earn a point when she or he held the serve. Susanti relied on deep clears to the back line, limiting the chance of a fast-paced exchange, mixed with tight drop shots, forcing her opponent to cover the entire court. Susanti frequently covered her backhand side with overhead forehands, by relying on her quickness and back-arching suppleness. Relatively short, she often stretched her legs very wide to take low shots at the corners or away from her position. Developed from training, this leg-stretching, almost balletic maneuver became a signature pose which sometimes ended with a full leg split. In the later years of her career, Susanti incorporated more smashing into her repertoire, enough to throw off opponents expecting only a game of attrition.

== Personal life ==
She is married to [[Alan Budikusuma]] ({{lang-zh|c=魏仁芳}}), a men's badminton Olympic gold medalist (also in 1992) and one of the top men's players in the history of the sport, a former [[Chinese Indonesian]] [[badminton]] player who excelled at the world level from the late 1980s to the mid-1990s.<ref>{{cite news |last=Clarey |first=Christopher |date=25 June 1996 |title=ATLANTA 1996 -- BADMINTON IN INDONESIA;This Is No Picnic: In Southeast Asia, Respect Rides on a Shuttlecock |newspaper=The New York Times |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1996/06/25/sports/atlanta-1996-badminton-indonesia-this-no-picnic-southeast-asia-respect-rides.html#h |url-status=live |url-access=limited |access-date=11 September 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180128021250/https://www.nytimes.com/1996/06/25/sports/atlanta-1996-badminton-indonesia-this-no-picnic-southeast-asia-respect-rides.html |archive-date=28 January 2018}}</ref> Together they have three children, Laurencia Averina, born 1999, Albertus Edward, born 2000, Sebastianus Fredrick, born 2003. When the eldest daughter was born, Indonesia was rocked by a series of civil outbreaks and violence. Susanti decided to name her daughter Laurencia Averina Wiratama, which means “peace”, hoping that she would bring about peace in the nation.<ref>{{cite web |last=Keong |first=Chia Han |date=6 July 2021 |title=Indonesia's Golden Couple who won badminton's first Olympic golds |url=https://sg.news.yahoo.com/indonesia-golden-couple-badmintons-first-olympic-golds-020631154.html |access-date=22 June 2022 |website=Yahoo! News |publisher=}}</ref>

==In popular culture==
A [[biopic]] in [[Indonesian language|Indonesian]] based on Susanti's life story, entitled ''[[Susi Susanti: Love All]]'' directed by Sim F with [[Laura Basuki]] playing the titular role and [[Dion Wiyoko]] as Alan Budikusuma was released on 24 October 2019.<ref>{{cite news|title='Susi Susanti – Love All' shows different side of legendary shuttler|url=https://www.thejakartapost.com/life/2019/10/17/biopic-susi-susanti-love-all-stays-true-to-real-life-events.html/|author=Ni Nyoman Wira|date=17 October 2018|work=The Jakarta Post|access-date=17 October 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|author=Indrasty|first=Rissa|date=19 September 2018|title=Ini Sisi Lain Yang Akan Diangkat di Film Susy Susanti - Love All|url=http://www.grid.id/read/04940927/ini-sisi-lain-yang-akan-diangkat-di-film-susy-susanti-love-all?page=all|publisher=Grid Network (Grid)|language=id|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190327085750/https://www.grid.id/read/04940927/ini-sisi-lain-yang-akan-diangkat-di-film-susy-susanti-love-all|archive-date=27 March 2019|accessdate=7 October 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|author=Pangerang|first=Andi Muttya Keteng|date=17 September 2018|editor=Dewi|editor-first=Bestari Kumala|title=Penampilan Perdana Laura Basuki sebagai Susy Susanti|url=https://entertainment.kompas.com/read/2018/09/17/163540110/penampilan-perdana-laura-basuki-sebagai-susy-susanti|website=|publisher=[[Kompas.com|Kompas]]|language=id|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181007184749/https://entertainment.kompas.com/read/2018/09/17/163540110/penampilan-perdana-laura-basuki-sebagai-susy-susanti|archive-date=7 October 2018|accessdate=7 October 2018}}</ref>

=== World Junior Championships ===
The [[Bimantara World Badminton Junior Invitation Championships|Bimantara World Junior Championships]] was an international invitation badminton tournament for junior players. It was held in Jakarta, Indonesia from 1987 to 1991.
